Subject: Recap: perf discovery — token profile & SLO mapping
Attachments: call_recording_030226.mp3, initial-workload-estimates.xlsx

Thanks again for the call earlier today — good conversation and helpful context. Short recap + proposed next steps so we can size a realistic offering and map to your SLOs.

High-level workload notes (from call):
- Steady-state baseline QPS: ~120 requests/sec (you mentioned 90–130 in the core window)
- Observed peak (marketing/launch bursts): up to ~450–480 QPS for short windows (1–10 min)
- Average tokens per request: ~420 tokens (median ~150, long-tail to ~2k on some endpoints)
- Streaming usage: ~55% of requests are streaming (primarily real-time transcription + progressive replies)
- Concurrent active streams during peak: ~180 concurrent sessions
- Aggregate tokens/sec: baseline ~50k t/s, peak bursts up to ~200k t/s (short spikes)

Target SLO constraints we discussed:
- Non-streaming end-to-end p95 latency target: <= 250 ms
- Streaming first-byte latency target: <= 120 ms; steady chunk delivery within 200 ms
- Availability: you requested 99.9% for public-facing endpoints

Immediate asks / data needed to size formally (action items):
1) Sample traffic capture (anonymized): ~1–2k requests representative across endpoints, plus a CSV of timestamped QPS by minute for the past 30 days. Prefer a link to a GCS/Drive folder.
2) A short list of 3 highest-volume endpoints and 2 high-tail endpoints (where token counts spike).
3) Confirmation on retention/compliance constraints (do you need private deployment / VPC?).
4) Any procurement threshold (Marissa, can you confirm contract review SLAs / PO process?)

What we propose next from Redwood:
- Quick sizing exercise + benchmark plan (we'll propose hardware permutations and a canary strategy focused on streaming-first latency).
- Preliminary cost/throughput envelope (we'll return expected t/s and token/unit cost bands).
- 30–45 minute follow-up to review the bench results and discuss rollout/fallback policies.

Proposed owners and ETA:
- Karthik: run initial sizing + coordinate bench (ETA 2 business days after samples)
- Aditya: run micro-bench and latency profiling on candidate configs (ETA 3 business days)
- Marissa: coordinate procurement questions and provide contract intake details (please confirm).

Uploading the two small attachments: call_recording_030226.mp3 (recording) and initial-workload-estimates.xlsx (our rough back-of-envelope). If you can upload the sample payloads and QPS CSV to the Drive link above, we'll start sizing.

Thanks — available for a quick sync tomorrow 10–12 PT or Thu 1–3 PT.

—

Thanks Karthik — great summary. A few clarifications based on the data we pulled post-call: 
- Baseline QPS during business hours is ~90 QPS (our earlier estimate included some background workloads). Please use 90 QPS as conservative baseline.
- Peak bursts: we've seen up to 3x baseline for some campaign-driven traffic (so ~270 QPS sustained for ~20–30 minutes) and short spikes to ~500 QPS for <2 minutes.
- Streaming: closer to 60% of user-facing requests, and streaming sessions average ~45s; concurrent stream estimate of 180 in peak aligns with our telemetry.
- Token distribution: median ~160, mean ~420, but a small set (~2%) of endpoints return 1k–2.5k tokens (reporting endpoints).

I've uploaded sample payloads and a minute-level QPS CSV to the GCS link below (public-read for now):
https://storage.googleapis.com/summitapps-bucket/samples/sample-payloads-030226.json

Two quick questions for you: 
1) For streaming-first-byte latency, how do you account for client-side throttling (we currently cap chunk size to 512 tokens)?
2) Does Redwood recommend an autoscaling headroom policy for scheduled campaigns (e.g., reserve 2x baseline for first 72 hrs during launch)?

Happy to hop on a follow-up — Thu 9–10 PT or Fri 11–1 PT works here.

Adding a few practical notes from infra/benchmark side:
- Given the token tail and streaming percentage, we'll prioritize a config that optimizes first-byte for streaming while keeping throughput cost reasonable. Candidate options: 8x A100 (mixed packing), 16x A10g with aggressive batching for non-streaming, and a quantized int8 combo for high-volume endpoints.
- For spikes we should validate two autoscale strategies:
  1) Pre-warm buffer: maintain 2x baseline pool during known campaigns (fastest ramp, predictable latency)
  2) Reactive burst + fallback: allow short burst to max capacity with automatic fallback to lower-cost model variant if SLOs risk being breached
- Benchmark plan (attached brief): microbench (90 QPS baseline x 30 min), burst test (simulate 3x baseline for 30 min), and spike test (simulate 500 QPS for 2 min). We'll collect p50/p95/p99 latency and first-byte for streams plus tokens/sec.

Requesting Leah: please upload the minute-level QPS CSV + anonymized sample payloads to the Drive link so we can use them directly in the synthetic runner. Also send a short list of the two endpoints that produce the long-tail token responses so we can run focused token-heavy trials.

Proposed sync: Thu 10:00–10:30 PT to align on bench scope; I'll own the microbench execution.

—
